title: Inference economics vertical canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operational canvas for ops-led GTM motions that foregrounds inference economics as the primary hook for regulated and cost-sensitive verticals (fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense). The goal is to produce repeatable messaging blocks, quick battlecards, and 3x testable experiments per vertical for the next quarter's field play.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
Position Redwood as the inference partner that lets platform and product teams deliver predictable, auditable LLM features at a sustainable cost. Lead with measurable economics (per-request token cost + unit-latency SLO), then layer in enterprise constraints: private deploy options, key management, and audit trails. For gov/defense and healthcare, emphasize controllability and verified fallback patterns; for fintech and enterprise SaaS emphasize latency SLAs and predictable throughput.

Target personas by vertical (who we actually talk to):
- Fintech: Platform engineering lead (latency, cost), Head of Prod/Payments (fraud/risk use cases), Compliance/Legal (data residency).
- Healthcare: Clinical informatics lead (data lineage), Security/compliance officer (PHI handling), DevOps/Platform (on-prem/VPC expectations).
- Legal: Knowledge-management/product owners (search/briefing productivity), Security counsel (privilege/data retention), Platform SRE.
- Enterprise SaaS: Product manager (feature velocity), Platform engineering (multi-tenant performance), Finance/Procurement (predictable spend).
- Gov/Defense: Chief Architect / Systems Integrator (air-gapped installs), CISO / Security reviewer (HSM/KMS, accreditation), Program manager (SLA/governance).

Core value pillars (short bullets for sales/AE scripts):
1) Predictable inference economics: we surface per-request cost, batch/carve options, and expose knobs (quantization, caching, batch windows) that directly map to $/100k requests.
2) Operational observability and auditing: token-level cost attribution, per-route tracing, request provenance for audits.
3) Deployment flexibility: hosted for fast pilots, dedicated for predictable commits, private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads.
4) Graceful degradation and policy controls: model variant fallback, region fallbacks, and automated routing policies to keep service available during capacity stress.
5) Platform-first SDKs and rollouts: canary/A-B rollout flows and guardrails for quality regressions tied to eval sets.

Leading messaging strings (frames to test):
- Economics-first hook: "Cut inference spend predictably — not just salable performance."
- Audit/control hook: "Ship LLM features with the same auditability and controls you expect from critical infra."
- Platform hook: "One runtime, same API — from pilot to air-gapped production."

Top objections we expect and quick rebuttals (AE cheatsheet):
- "We can self-host and save money": Rebuttal: Short-term token cost reduction vs long-term ops burden. Show total cost of ownership (engineering hours, reliability incidents, opportunity cost). Offer a POC comparing end-to-end ops metrics.
- "Public APIs are simpler": Rebuttal: Simpler until you need auditability, predictable throughput, or data residency. We can start hosted and migrate to private with the same API.
- "Latency matters more than cost": Rebuttal: Show how batching, region routing, and dedicated pools hit latency SLOs while also controlling cost. Provide prior benchmark artifacts and trace examples.

Competitive notes (high-level, for enablement):
- Open incumbents (broad API providers): Pros: developer mindshare, simple surface. Cons: limited private deployment options, less tooling for per-token cost attribution, weaker rollout controls.
- Cloud-native offerings (cloud vendor managed endpoints): Pros: strong infra integration, single-vendor procurement. Cons: configuration sprawl, limited inference-specific optimizations and poor cost visibility per model/request.
- OSS/self-host runtimes: Pros: price control, flexibility. Cons: heavy ops burden, no turnkey audit trails, slower time-to-value.

Short battlecards (phrased for AE):
- Against "Public API provider X": "We match the dev ergonomics you like but add dedicated capacity, per-route cost dashboards, and model fallbacks so you can meet financial procurement and audit checks without building a separate stack."
- Against "Cloud managed endpoints": "They win on billing consolidation; we win on inference economics visibility and model-aware kernel selection that reduces token costs and improves tail latency."
- Against "Self-hosted stack": "We remove months of infra work and ongoing pager burden; we also provide a migration path and private deployment so you keep control without rebuilding a runtime."

Vertical-specific hooks and deployment plays (quick sketch):
- Fintech: pilot with fraud detection reranker — measure cost/latency of re-ranking 100–200 calls/sec; show routing to dedicated pool to keep 99th percentile latency < 75ms. Bring compliance by showing private VPC with KMS and audit trails for sample transactions.
- Healthcare: start with clinician summarization in a VPC pilot; instrument PHI tagging + retention policies; surface lineage for each generated item. Emphasize certs and SOC/ISO talk track.
- Legal: knowledge search + brief generation. Sell on repeatable quality monitoring (evals tied to canonical prompt sets) and near-zero leakage guarantees with private deploys.
- Enterprise SaaS: multi-tenant embeddings + reranking. Offer shareable per-tenant cost dashboards and an autoscaling policy that isolates noisy tenants.
- Gov/Defense: air-gapped deploy trial with discrete hardware images, HSM/KMS integrations, and documented accreditation checklist (NIST/CMMC style language).

Experiment matrix (3 experiments per vertical, short):
- Fintech: 1) Cost-first email campaign with a linked calculator (A/B cost figure presentation). 2) Technical brief + benchmark PDF. 3) Hands-on lab with a data-shielded fraud reranker (invite-only).
- Healthcare: 1) Technical webinar on PHI handling and lineage. 2) Case study stub with clinical informatics partner. 3) Workshop: mapping clinical workflows to private deployment patterns.
- Legal: 1) Productized eval kit for brief quality regression. 2) Partner co-sell with KM vendor. 3) One-pager on retention and privilege controls.
- Enterprise SaaS: 1) ROI calculator for feature adoption speed vs cost. 2) Demo showing per-tenant chargeback reporting. 3) SRE-focused checklist for rollout.
- Gov/Defense: 1) Security-only brief for PMO/CISO. 2) Offline installer demo (air-gap proof-of-concept). 3) Procurement play template with sample contract language.

Metrics we want to move (KPIs for the campaign):
- # of pilot leads that request private deployment POC.
- Time from first contact to pilot activation (goal: < 14 days).
- Conversion rate from pilot to paid committed capacity deals.
- Reduction in customer-reported inference unit cost vs their baseline after 90 days.

Open questions / discussion items (for next sync):
- What benchmark artifacts are most convincing for fintech fraud/latency comparisons? Who on infra owns production-grade benchmarks?
- For gov play, what legal templates do we already have vs what needs creation?
- Need a short PHI compliance checklist we can hand to prospects (owner: Ananya?).

Next steps (concrete):
- Build one-pager templates per vertical and test the cost-first subject line variant in email outreach (owner: Marcus).
- Assemble a benchmark pack (end-to-end traces, cost per 100k requests, tail latency) for the fintech and SaaS plays (owner: Serving Runtime team liaison).
- Draft gov/defense procurement play and air-gap checklist (owner: Diego).

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Consider a small interactive calculator on the site where a prospect enters throughput, average prompt size, and desired p99 latency — returns recommended pool config and estimated monthly spend.
- Link quickstart repo to a sanitized fintech demo dataset for rapid hands-on labs.

End of canvas.
